newsitem.title: UK: Palladium fixed at $161.50, highest since May 1995.
newsitem.headline: Palladium fixed at $161.50, highest since May 1995.

text.p: Palladium fixed at $161.50 an ounce in London on Friday, the highest fixing since 31 May 1995 and $2.50 above the the earlier fixing.
Fears of further delays in shipments from the world's biggest exporter, Russia, is keeping the market tight, dealers said.
Friday's fix was the strongest since May 31, 1995, when it came in at $162.00.
Earlier this month, palladium surged to fix at $160.25 on April 10.

No news has yet emerged on when Russia would resume exports to Japan, the world's largest importer of platinum group metals (PGM), after contractual talks between the two countries hit what is said to be bureaucratic snags in Moscow.
Dealers noted intense buying of palladium on Friday, which helped the spot rates jump as much as $3.50 to just below $160.00 an ounce.
By 1330 GMT the rare white metal was indicated at $160.75/161.75, up $5.00 from Thursday's European close.
Palladium is mainly used in electronics and autocatalysts.

Market players are worried that recently unveiled plans by Moscow to overhaul the the way in which it markets precious metals, possibly with larger hard currency earnings in mind, could result in longer delays.
Palladium's sister metal platinum was quoted at $378.50/$379.50, up $2.50, as it chased palladium's gains. It fixed at $379.35 an ounce, compared with the previous fix of $377.00.
